description: How machines measure the physical world and act on it: sensing principles and sensor characteristics, position, speed and distance sensors, inertial and environmental sensors, signal conditioning and data conversion, DC, stepper and servo motors, motor drivers and power electronics, and the basics of fusing several sensors into one estimate. Practised in browser-based circuit and motor simulations with virtual instruments, building towards field devices such as soil-moisture irrigation controllers and line-following delivery robots.
modelledOn: Fraden, Handbook of Modern Sensors: Physics, Designs, and Applications
Bolton, Mechatronics: Electronic Control Systems in Mechanical and Electrical Engineering
Hughes and Drury, Electric Motors and Drives: Fundamentals, Types and Applications
Horowitz and Hill, The Art of Electronics
outcomes: Explain the physical principles behind common transducers and characterise a sensor by its range, sensitivity, resolution, accuracy, linearity and dynamic response.
Select and interface position, speed, distance, inertial and environmental sensors for a given measurement task and calibrate them.
Design signal conditioning circuits with bridges, amplifiers and filters and choose sampling rates and ADC resolution to avoid aliasing and quantisation error.
Model DC, stepper and servo motors and select a motor and gearing from torque, speed and power requirements.
Design motor drive circuits with H-bridges, PWM and protection and size power supplies and batteries for a mobile system.
Combine readings from several sensors with complementary and Kalman filters to estimate orientation and position.

units.title: Sensing principles
topics: Measurement systems: transducer, conditioning, conversion, processing; sensors and actuators in a control loop
Physical effects used in sensing: resistive, capacitive, inductive, piezoelectric, thermoelectric, photoelectric, Hall effect
Static characteristics: range, sensitivity, resolution, accuracy, precision, linearity, hysteresis, offset and drift
Dynamic characteristics: first- and second-order response, time constant, bandwidth, settling time
Errors and uncertainty: systematic and random error, noise, calibration curves and least-squares fitting
Reading sensor datasheets and choosing a sensor against cost, power and environment

units.title: Position, speed and distance sensors
topics: Potentiometers, limit switches and Hall effect position sensing
Rotary and linear encoders: incremental quadrature decoding, absolute encoders, counts per revolution
Speed measurement from encoder pulses, tachogenerators and frequency or period counting
Distance sensing: ultrasonic time of flight, infrared triangulation, optical time-of-flight and lidar in outline
Proximity and line sensors: inductive, capacitive and reflective optical; a line-following array for a delivery robot
Error sources: echo dropouts, temperature effects on the speed of sound, surface reflectivity

units.title: Inertial and environmental sensors
topics: MEMS accelerometers and gyroscopes: proof masses, capacitive sensing, bias, noise density and drift
Magnetometers and compass heading; hard- and soft-iron calibration
Temperature sensing: thermistors, RTDs, thermocouples with cold-junction compensation, digital sensors
Humidity, pressure, light and gas sensors; soil moisture by resistive and capacitive probes
Strain gauges and load cells for weighing produce; the Wheatstone bridge
Sensors for agriculture and weather stations in Ghana: rainfall gauges, soil moisture and grain storage monitoring

units.title: Signal conditioning
topics: Voltage dividers, bridges and current loops (4-20 mA) for industrial sensors
Operational amplifier circuits: inverting, non-inverting, differential and instrumentation amplifiers
Analogue filtering: passive and active RC filters, anti-aliasing filter design
Sampling and the Nyquist criterion; ADC resolution, reference voltage, quantisation noise, oversampling
Digital filtering of sensor data: moving average, exponential smoothing, median filters
Noise, grounding, shielding and protection against ESD and overvoltage

units.title: DC, stepper and servo motors
topics: Electromagnetic principles: force on a conductor, back EMF, torque constant
Brushed DC motors: equivalent circuit, torque-speed curve, efficiency, transfer function model
Brushless DC motors and electronic commutation in outline
Stepper motors: permanent-magnet and hybrid types, full, half and microstepping, holding torque, missed steps
RC servos and closed-loop position control; PID control of motor speed in outline
Gearing, inertia matching and selecting a motor for a robot wheel or irrigation valve; solenoids and relays as actuators

units.title: Motor drivers and power
topics: Switching loads with transistors and MOSFETs; flyback diodes and inductive kickback
H-bridges for direction and braking; PWM speed control, switching frequency and current ripple
Stepper drivers with current chopping; integrated driver ICs and their thermal limits
Current sensing, overcurrent and thermal protection; electrical noise from motors
Power supplies, regulators and batteries: capacity, discharge rates, lithium and lead-acid chemistries
Solar power budgeting for an off-grid pump or sensor node

units.title: Sensor fusion basics and project
topics: Why fuse sensors: complementary strengths and uncorrelated errors
Complementary filter for tilt from an accelerometer and gyroscope
The one-dimensional Kalman filter: prediction, update, covariance; tuning noise parameters
Dead reckoning from wheel encoders corrected with other sensors
Project: a sensing and actuation system such as an automatic irrigation controller or a small delivery robot with odometry

schedule.title: Measurement systems and static characteristics
schedule.exercise: Problem set: from a calibration table of a pressure sensor, compute range, sensitivity, linearity error, hysteresis and resolution, and state which characteristic limits accuracy most.

tasks.title: Compute sensitivity, offset and linearity error from a ten-point calibration table of a temperature sensor and plot the fit
Wire a thermistor to an Arduino analogue pin, read it through the serial monitor, and show the signal path from sensor to number
Choose the best sensing principle for six field measurements in a branching case, balancing accuracy, power and cost against the rubric

schedule.title: Dynamic response, errors and datasheets
schedule.exercise: Estimate the time constant of a temperature probe from a step test, compute its 95 percent settling time, and propose a correction for the lag.

tasks.title: Fit a first-order step response to measured data and read the time constant and the 95 percent settling time
Fit a least-squares calibration line to noisy data, report its slope and intercept uncertainties, and plot the residuals
Select between two soil moisture sensors from their datasheets for a battery-powered node, then wire and read the chosen one

schedule.title: Position, speed and rotation sensing
schedule.exercise: Compute the resolution and maximum speed of a 1000-count quadrature encoder, and design a method to measure low and high speeds accurately.

tasks.title: Read a quadrature encoder with two Arduino pins and display the position count as the shaft turns
Measure motor speed from encoder pulses using frequency counting and period counting, and compare the accuracy of the two at low and high speed
Fix an encoder reader that loses counts at high speed by moving to interrupts, and verify zero missed counts over 10000 pulses

schedule.title: Distance, proximity and line sensing
schedule.exercise: Compute how the speed of sound changes with temperature and the resulting distance error of an ultrasonic sensor at 15 and 40 degrees Celsius.

tasks.title: Read an ultrasonic sensor's echo time, convert it to distance, and compare readings at five known distances
Correct an ultrasonic distance reading for air temperature and test the error with and without correction at 40 degrees
Build a line-following array reading with weighted-position calculation for a delivery robot, and verify the position estimate on a curved line

schedule.title: Inertial, thermal and magnetic sensors
schedule.exercise: Calibrate a magnetometer from sample data by estimating hard-iron offsets, and explain how soft-iron distortion changes the plotted circle.

tasks.title: Read a digital temperature sensor over I2C and compare it with a thermistor reading at three temperatures
Measure accelerometer bias and noise from 1000 samples at rest and report the bias and the noise standard deviation
Calibrate a magnetometer by fitting an offset and scale to rotated data, and compute heading error before and after

schedule.title: Environmental sensors and weighing
schedule.exercise: Design a weather station for a Ghanaian farm: list the sensors, ranges, power budget and the placement of each, and the calibration needed.

tasks.title: Read a capacitive soil moisture sensor, calibrate it with dry and wet samples, and convert readings to percent moisture
Compute the Wheatstone bridge output for a load cell under five loads and fit a calibration line to read weight
Build a grain-store monitor that reads temperature and humidity, publishes readings, and raises an alert when spoilage conditions are met

schedule.title: Signal conditioning circuits
schedule.exercise: Design an instrumentation amplifier stage for a 0 to 20 mV bridge output into a 0 to 3.3 V ADC, giving the gain, resistor values and expected error.

tasks.title: Build a 4-20 mA current loop receiver with a 250 ohm resistor and verify the voltage at 4, 12 and 20 mA
Design a differential amplifier stage that scales a 0 to 20 mV bridge signal to 0 to 3.3 V, and measure its gain and error
Design an active anti-aliasing filter for a 1 kHz ADC rate and verify that a 3 kHz interference tone is attenuated by at least 40 dB

schedule.title: Sampling, digital filtering and noise control
schedule.exercise: Compare moving average, exponential smoothing and median filtering on a noisy signal with spikes, and recommend a filter for each of three sensors.

tasks.title: Sample a 100 Hz sine at three rates, show aliasing in the sampled values, and choose a safe rate
Filter a noisy analogue reading on an Arduino with a moving average and an exponential filter, and compare noise and lag
Reduce the noise on a sensor reading disturbed by a nearby motor by changing grounding, filtering and shielding, and measure the improvement in standard deviation

schedule.title: Electromagnetic principles and DC motors
schedule.exercise: Derive the torque-speed line of a brushed motor from its equivalent circuit, compute stall torque and no-load speed, and identify the peak-efficiency point.

tasks.title: Plot the torque-speed and efficiency curves of a brushed DC motor from its constants and mark the stall point
Model a DC motor's transfer function from its constants and plot the speed step response and time constant
Choose between brushed and brushless motors for a pump and a robot wheel in a branching case, weighing efficiency, cost and electronics

schedule.title: Steppers, servos and motor selection
schedule.exercise: Select a motor and gearbox for a robot wheel from torque, speed and voltage requirements, showing the calculation and the safety margin.

tasks.title: Drive a stepper motor in full-step and half-step modes from an Arduino and count the steps for one revolution
Tune a PID controller for motor speed using encoder feedback in the simulator and record the overshoot and settling time
Size a motor and gearbox for an irrigation valve or a robot wheel from the load torque, speed and inertia, and justify the selection

schedule.title: Driving loads and motor power electronics
schedule.exercise: Design a motor driver for a 12 V motor: choose the transistor or H-bridge, flyback protection and PWM frequency, and give the expected switching loss.

tasks.title: Switch a 12 V load with a MOSFET controlled by an Arduino pin and add a flyback diode across an inductive load
Control motor speed and direction with an H-bridge and PWM from an Arduino, and plot speed against duty cycle
Configure a stepper driver with current chopping to avoid missed steps at higher speed, and check the driver temperature against its limit

schedule.title: Protection, power and batteries
schedule.exercise: Prepare a power budget for a solar-powered sensor node, including load currents, duty cycle, battery capacity for three cloudy days and panel size.

tasks.title: Measure the current drawn by a motor and trip an overcurrent cut-off when it passes a threshold
Compute battery runtime for a sensor node at several duty cycles, including self-discharge, and compare lithium and lead-acid choices
Size the panel and battery for an off-grid pump or sensor node over three cloudy days, and test the design against a month of weather data

schedule.title: Sensor fusion and final project
schedule.exercise: Project proposal: specify the sensors, actuators, filters, control logic and test plan for an automatic irrigation controller or a delivery robot with odometry.

tasks.title: Combine two noisy sensors measuring the same quantity by weighted averaging and show that fused error is smaller than either input's
Fuse accelerometer and gyroscope readings with a complementary filter to estimate tilt, and tune the blend to reject vibration and drift
Build an automatic irrigation controller with a soil moisture sensor, pump relay and logging, and test it over simulated wet and dry days
